verdict: The spoken core here is genuinely good and in places better than any textbook: короче, ну, бывает, потихоньку, обиделся, разувайтесь, тапочки, "телефон сел", "ну всё, давай, пока", the кухня-as-social-centre note and the men-shake-hands-but-never-across-a-threshold note are exactly what a British adult needs to sound like a person rather than a phrasebook, and the register calls (ты/вы, patronymics, name diminutives, извините vs простите) are sound. Three systemic faults hold it back. First, duplication: I count roughly sixty repeated teachables (сметана three times, девушка and молодой человек three times each at three different tiers, чай будешь, мне пора, сколько времени, может быть, кажется, слушай, сюда/туда, дядя/тётя, блины, пирожок, плов, зарядка, звонок, пробка, взять трубку, and the two tier-1 aspect paradigms hs-0181 and hs-0669), so 1,154 items is closer to 1,050 real ones and the tier assignments of the copies contradict each other. Second, the Hindi scaffolding is still load-bearing and still user-visible: a dozen notes contain Devanagari a Russian learner cannot read (भाभी, हाथ, हम लोग, ससुराल, जी, पूजा, आशीर्वाद, होटल), a dozen more compare the language to paneer, paratha, thali, masala, mango, cricket, kurta and auto-rickshaws, and the tiering still walks a Hindi day rather than a Russian one, which is why rice sits at tier 2 while the syllabus has no до свидания, no добрый день, no нельзя, no age question, and not one word for beer, wine or the toasting ritual that structures every Russian evening. Third, and most damaging for a beginner, there is no pronunciation or prosody layer at all: nothing on stress and о-reduction, nothing on hard versus soft consonants even though ь changes брат into брать, and nothing on the fact that a yes/no question is marked by intonation alone. Smaller defects: the note on hs-0076 belongs to знать, hs-0416's plural examples (дома, окна) contradict the -ы/-и rule it states, hs-0030 romanises -ют as "-ut", and the romanisation scheme itself changes twice mid-file (no soft-sign apostrophes before hs-0392, apostrophes through hs-0771, then dropped again). Fix the pronunciation gap, dedupe, strip the Hindi comparanda, and add the missing day-one social frames and this is a strong, unusually idiomatic 1,000-item Russian spine.

items.en: is – not said in the present
items.note: Russian has no present-tense 'is/am/are'. Он врач = he's a doctor. In writing a dash stands in: Москва – столица.
нет = 'no' and 'there isn't'; не goes straight in front of the word you negate: я не знаю.
Capitalised Вы in letters and messages to one person.
The one surviving present form of быть, kept only for existence and possession: у меня есть время. Never for plain 'X is Y'.
Это + noun opens the sentences where English needs 'is': Это моя сестра. The adjective form is этот / эта / эти.
Every object is he or she too: стол – он, книга – она.
машина брата = my brother's car. The owner takes the ending, the order is thing-then-owner.
в доме = in the house (prepositional); в дом, в Москву = into / to (accusative). Where-at vs where-to changes the case, not the preposition.
скажи брату = tell my brother. Also carries feelings and needs: мне холодно, мне нравится.
из Лондона (out of), с работы (off/from), от мамы (from a person). All take the genitive.
на столе = on the table; на работу = to work. Some places take на rather than в: на почте, на вокзале.
а is the contrasting 'and/but': я иду, а ты?
The all-purpose spoken opener: ну ладно, ну и что, ну давай.
привет to friends and family, здравствуйте to anyone else. Здрасьте is the mumbled everyday version.
Learn both halves from day one: делать for the doing, сделать for the done.
Only its past (был) and future (буду) are actually said; the present is zero.
идти on foot, ехать by any vehicle. Getting this wrong is the classic giveaway.

items.en: to come; to arrive on foot
items.note: приходи! = come round! приезжай! if they'd be travelling.

items.en: present tense: я делаю = I do AND I'm doing
items.note: Second pattern: -ю / -ишь / -ит / -им / -ите / -ят (говорю, говоришь). One present tense covers both English presents.

items.en: to me; me (with like, need, feel)
items.note: Dative. Carries most feeling-sentences: мне нравится, мне нужно, мне холодно.
где = where at, куда = where to: куда ты идёшь?
зачем = what for, with a hint of 'what's the point'.
Takes the genitive after it: сколько времени, сколько людей.
тут is the everyday spoken 'here'. иди сюда = come here.
Spoken as щас. On its own it means 'hang on, coming'.
For 'right now' Russians simply say сейчас or прямо сейчас.
Unlike Hindi, Russian keeps them separate – no one word for both.
всё! on its own = that's it, done.
все = everyone, всё (neuter) = everything. One letter apart, said differently: vse / vsyo.
что-нибудь = anything, in questions and offers: хочешь что-нибудь?
Singular is человек, which also counts people: пять человек.
как дела? = how are things; в чём дело? = what's the matter.
на работе = at work, на работу = to work – this one takes на, not в.
дома = at home, домой = homewards. Most 'houses' are flats.
фамилия = surname. Neuter and slightly irregular.
Black, with lemon or jam. Milk in tea will raise eyebrows.
'to eat' is есть, irregular: ем, ешь, ест, едим, едите, едят. Кушать is what you say to a guest or a child – я кушаю about yourself sounds twee.
Neuter, and grows an -ен- in other cases: сколько времени.
штука is the casual 'thing, item'.
The two halves look nothing alike – learn them as a pair.
смотреть = look at deliberately, видеть = see, perceive.

items.en: to speak; to talk; to say
items.note: я говорю по-русски.
The perfective partner of говорить: скажи мне = tell me.
давай встретимся = let's meet up. Meeting someone for the first time is познакомиться.
Russian addresses run big to small: город, улица, дом, квартира. Дай мне свой адрес.
я живу в Лондоне. 'to stay' is оставаться.
мне надо идти = I have to go. надо is the everyday one, нужно slightly tidier.
The round-trip partners of идти / ехать: я хожу на работу = I go to work every day.
'to make' in general is делать; готовить is for food and for getting things ready.
ставить / поставить for anything that stands upright. Russians care which.

items.en: imperative: bare form for ты, + -те for вы
items.note: иди / идите, скажи / скажите, подожди / подождите. The -те is the polite plural.
пойдём and поехали do the same job. давай alone = go on then, and also 'bye' on the phone.
заходи / заходите = drop in, come round.
присаживайтесь is softer; садитесь alone is fine among friends.

items.en: please take it; here you are
items.note: Handing something over: вот, пожалуйста, or держи to a friend.
слушаю вас is the phone and counter version.
The one for getting attention or squeezing past.
Heavier than извините – use it when you actually did something.

items.en: please; you're welcome; here you are
items.note: Said 'pazhalsta' – the middle of the word disappears in speech.
The reply to an apology. Ничего! on its own works too.
Russian has no polite 'yes' – да covers every level. ага is the casual yeah.
You will need it repeatedly at a Russian table.
Unlike the English version this expects a real answer, not 'fine'.
Literally 'they call me'.
как тебя зовут? to someone your own age or younger.
Literally 'I want to eat'. я голодный / голодная also works.
а for a softer contrast: я пойду, а ты оставайся.
эй! to call out to someone.
две with feminine nouns. Numbers bend the noun: 2-4 take the genitive singular (два часа), 5+ the genitive plural (пять часов).
No older/younger split: старший брат, младший брат.

items.en: excuse me, miss (addressing a young woman)
items.note: Russian never uses kin terms for strangers. Девушка! is how you get a waitress's or shop assistant's attention.

items.en: excuse me, mate (addressing a young man)
items.note: The male counterpart of девушка. Мужчина! exists but sounds blunt.

items.en: do you want something to eat?
items.note: Not a greeting in Russian, but it carries the same warmth: a host asks this within a minute of you arriving.
Say понял if you're a man, поняла if you're a woman – the past tense is gendered.
не поняла if you're a woman.

items.en: how do you say this in Russian?

items.note: по-русски with verbs of speaking; русский язык as the noun.
для меня = for me, + genitive. 'For' in the sense of fetching is за: пошёл за хлебом.
Takes the instrumental: с другом, с мамой. A bare instrumental means 'using': ножом = with a knife.
у меня, у него, у Ани. Also 'round at': у нас дома.
я могу, ты можешь. 'Can' as a learnt skill is уметь; 'may I?' is можно?
в час, в два часа, в пять часов – the number decides the ending.
A real aunt only. Calling a stranger тётя is either childish or rude.
Same rule as тётя: family only.
парень is a young man, and also 'boyfriend'.
девушка is also 'girlfriend', the way парень is 'boyfriend'. девочка is a child.
человек = person, in general.
выключить for switching something off.
Also да? – Russians often just answer with да.
Takes the dative: позвони мне.

items.en: to talk; to have a conversation
items.note: поговорить = to have a word about something.
Black rye bread is the default; чёрный / белый.
Lunch starts with it. борщ and щи are the classics.
Russian food is mild, so you'll need this less than you think.
обед = lunch (the big meal), ужин = supper.
A Russian host presses food on you exactly like a Hindi one. ещё чаю? = more tea?
ванная is the room with the bath in it, not the loo.
один рубль, два рубля, пять рублей.
подожди to a friend. Стойте! = stop!
наверное = probably, and is used far more.
Back to front: the thing liked is the subject. Мне нравится этот город = I like this city.
просто скажи = just say it; я просто устал = I'm just tired. просто так = for no particular reason.
в России = in Russia, в Россию = to Russia.

items.en: aspect: every verb comes as a pair
items.note: Imperfective for the process or the habit, perfective for the finished result: я делал (was doing) vs я сделал (got it done). This is the single biggest thing in Russian.
The standard reply to как дела?
большое спасибо = thanks a lot.
кушайте! is the homelier 'eat up'.
нужен agrees with the thing needed: мне нужен билет, мне нужна помощь.

items.en: to love; to like a lot
items.note: я люблю чай is perfectly ordinary – no romance implied with things.
понятия не имею = haven't the foggiest.
из Великобритании for the whole UK; Russians usually say Англия regardless.
No verb needed: Алло, это Джон.
Warm but slightly weighty. Friends just say давай, пока!
The first thing said to a guest in almost every Russian home.
Plural is дети, a different word altogether.
картофель is the shop and menu word; nobody says it at home.
ты with friends, family and children; вы with everyone else and for more than one person. Switching to ты is a small social event – let the Russian offer it.
The standard answer to спасибо, along with пожалуйста.
такое adds the raised eyebrow.
The food adjustment you'll actually need in Russia is leaving something out: без лука, без майонеза.
который час? is the tidier version.
Spoken Russian clips the final -а when you call someone: мам, Саш, Тань. It's the closest thing Russian has to a vocative.

items.en: name + patronymic: the respectful way to address someone
items.note: Father's name + -ович / -овна. Used for teachers, doctors, in-laws and anyone senior, always with вы.
Literally 'by me there is'. Drop есть when the point is what kind: у меня красная машина.

items.en: there isn't any; I haven't got
items.note: The missing thing goes into the genitive: у меня нет времени, его нет дома.
Pointing in a shop: вот этот, пожалуйста.
слушайте if you're on вы. Opens half of all spoken sentences.
ты же знаешь = but you know that. Hard to translate, easy to hear, and it makes you sound native.
There is no continuous tense in Russian. The plain present covers it, with сейчас added if you need to insist.
я был в Москве, было вкусно, их не было. Marked for gender, not for person.
Does the work of English 'who/which/that' in the middle of a sentence: человек, который живёт здесь.
просить / попросить = to ask FOR something. Two different verbs.
мне кажется, что ... = I reckon. Softer than я думаю.
The -ся ending means the action comes back on you. сидеть = to be sitting already.

items.en: to get up; to stand up

items.note: не надо! on its own = don't. Or не + imperative: не говори так.
The workhorse shop and cafe request: дайте, пожалуйста, воды.

items.en: excuse me, could you tell me ...
items.note: The standard way to open a question to a stranger in the street.
нравятся if the thing liked is plural: мне нравятся эти песни.
в смысле is the more casual 'I mean'.
Use свой when the owner is the subject: я взял свою книгу (mine) vs я взял его книгу (his).

items.en: adjectives agree in gender, number and case
items.note: новый дом, новая машина, новое место, новые люди. Every adjective, every time.
Russian encodes warmth in the name form, not in plural verbs: Александр → Саша → Сашенька. Friends always use the short one.

items.en: until; up to; as far as
past tense: я делал / она делала / они делали
items.note: Marked for gender and number but not person – я, ты and он all take делал. Far simpler than the present.

items.en: future: two ways, one per aspect
items.note: Imperfective takes буду + infinitive (буду читать); perfective just uses the present endings (прочитаю).

items.en: six cases: one noun, six endings
items.note: The ending shows the job the noun is doing, so word order is free. The six are nominative, genitive, dative, accusative (стол, same as the nominative for things), instrumental and prepositional.
давай + we-form for suggestions (давай выпьем чаю), можно for asking leave (можно войти?).
Two words, no verb. мне пора идти spells it out.
Genitive after можно when you mean 'some of it': можно чаю, можно хлеба.
до обеда = before lunch (any time earlier); перед обедом = right before it.
Russian doubles its negatives and must: я никогда не был в Москве.
Needs its не: я ничего не знаю. Ничего! on its own = never mind, it's fine.
Also the full-stop word: всё! = that's it, we're done.
два часа means both 'two hours' and 'two o'clock'.
один год, два года, пять лет – the plural switches to a different word entirely.
The -ом ending is the instrumental doing time duty: утром, вечером, ночью.

items.en: day after tomorrow / day before yesterday

items.note: полчаса, полкило, полдня – пол- glues straight onto the noun.
тёща is the wife's mother, свекровь the husband's. The тёща joke is a whole genre.
тесть = wife's father, свёкор = husband's father.

items.en: daughter-in-law (son's wife); also a brother's wife
items.note: A reference label, not a form of address – you call her by name.
Irregular plural of ребёнок.
жениться if you're the man, выйти замуж if you're the woman.
учиться = to be a student; заниматься = to do one's studying.

items.en: to go out; to set off; to get off

items.note: приходить if arriving on foot.
Takes the dative: помоги мне.
стараться = to make an effort. попробуй! also = give it a taste.
The -ся means it starts by itself: фильм начинается. Without it, начинать means you start something.
вас не слышно on вы. плохая связь = bad line.
по + dative. Said warmly to friends as well as partners.
наелась if you're a woman. You will need this – the plate keeps refilling.
маршрутка is the shared minibus that stops wherever you ask.
No rickshaws; everyone orders a car through an app. Indeclinable.
вокзал is a mainline terminus, станция a metro or local stop. остановка is a bus stop.
налево = left, направо = right.
недорого is the polite way to say cheap without the sneer.
жарко = it's hot out. горячий is hot to the touch.
холодно = it's cold (weather), мне холодно = I'm cold.
For broken things say не работает = it's not working, or сломался.
рад тебя видеть = good to see you. счастливый is 'happy' in the big, life-sized sense.
Said 'kaneshna'. One of the most common words in the language.
Also 'are you sure?': точно? совсем нет = absolutely not.
да ладно! = you're joking.
так вкусно! = so tasty; такой большой = such a big one. так goes with verbs and adverbs, такой with nouns.
круто! = cool; вау is the borrowed one younger people use.
не волнуйтесь on вы; не переживай is warmer still.

items.en: how did you like it?; what did you make of it?

items.note: с днём рождения! = happy birthday. Never congratulate a Russian early – it's bad luck.
Russians use first names far more than vocatives. блин is the filler exclamation that peppers speech (a mild 'damn').
за здоровье! is the toast everyone knows.
аптека = chemist's, and they'll advise you over the counter.
у меня болит голова = my head hurts. болит is the word you'll actually say.

items.en: to rest; to relax; to be on holiday

items.note: зимой = in winter; простуда is a cold, the illness. The one season everyone talks about.
идёт дождь = it's raining. снег (snow) will come up far more often.
дача is the country cottage half the country escapes to at weekends.
выходные = the weekend; каникулы = school and university holidays.
After a preposition they grow an н-: к нему, с ней.
The same word as the question: когда я приду, позвоню.
Literally 'on the street', and used for weather too: на улице холодно.
близко / недалеко = near. далеко отсюда? = is it far from here?
Unlike Hindi, Russian doesn't split them by side of the family – one pair of words covers all four.
идти в гости = to go visiting, в гостях = at someone's place. Never turn up empty-handed.
What you bring to the house, along with торт (cake) or flowers.
The default fruit, the way mango is in India.
The Russian table's masala: a spoonful goes into soup, onto pelmeni, onto almost everything.
Where Russian friendship happens – the real conversations are all at the kitchen table.
вегетарианка if you're a woman. Постное (Lenten food) is the practical fallback in a canteen.
One word covers the whole arm, shoulder to fingertips; взять за руку = to take by the hand.
Also covers both foot and leg.
Spoken Russian says 'у меня температура'. жар is literary.
A woman says устала – past-tense forms carry gender.
Fuller: я плохо себя чувствую.
Imperfective показывать.
Laundry is стирать, not мыть.
One specific trip is ехать/поехать; 'at the wheel' is за рулём.
Very colloquial with friends; neutral option is ладно, проехали.
Everyday short form телик.
Telegram fills the WhatsApp slot in Russia; ватсап is second.
'Скинь сообщение' – drop me a message.
весь день all day; целый = an entire one.
For the 'no worries' sense Russians say ничего страшного.

items.en: any chance of a bit cheaper?
items.note: Haggling is normal only at markets; shop prices are fixed.
By vehicle: поехали.

items.en: 'I have / I've got' frame: у меня температура, у меня вопрос
items.note: Russian has no verb 'to have'. This frame is day one, far earlier than in Hindi.
With friends: класс, круто, супер.

items.en: how much do I owe you?

items.note: Который час? is the formal version.
Also 'next' in a sequence.

items.en: noun gender by ending: consonant m, -а/-я f, -о/-е n, -ь can be either; plural -ы/-и for m and f (столы, книги) but -а for neuter (окна)
items.note: Gender drives adjective and past-tense agreement, so this comes first in Russian, not in month one.
Literally 'come through'; заходите is the invitation to visit.
Polite: кем вы работаете? Casual alternative: чем занимаешься?
в + prepositional for location: в Москве, в Лондоне.
Neutral: до встречи.
For 'I remember' use the verb помнить, not this noun.
про фильм is the spoken form; о фильме (+ prepositional) is neutral-formal.
'Это место свободно?' – is this seat taken?

items.en: to be late, be running late
items.note: Поезд опаздывает – the train is delayed.
For a device that is off, выключен.
Full form килограмм.
The goods go into the genitive: килограмм помидоров, полкило сыра.
Uncountable in Russian; 'an onion' is луковица.
The cashier's version is 'помельче не будет?'. Cards dominate, so this comes up less than in India.
Invitation to speak among friends; in a shop or office it is 'слушаю вас'.
Imperfective останавливаться.

items.en: to finish, be over, run out
items.note: Молоко закончилось – we're out of milk.
If the thing itself went missing: потерялся.
Also a hotel room.
In speech people use the verb: болит голова.

items.en: I think something disagreed with me
items.note: The standard way to say your stomach is upset; literally 'I've been poisoned'.
Два раза – twice; ещё раз – once more.
Rent is аренда or, for a flat, квартплата.
A city street is улица.
Power cuts are far rarer than in India, so this drops down the list.
Heating, not cooling, is the Russian household worry.
Мыть посуду – to do the washing-up.
The everyday fresh-cheese staple that paneer occupies in Hindi.
Plural яйца.
The cultured dairy that goes on everything, as dahi does; кефир to drink, йогурт is a shop product.
Imperfective забывать.

items.en: pronoun case forms: он – его – ему – им, она – её – ей – ей
items.note: Prepositions and verbs each demand a specific case, so these forms are needed from week one, not month two.
Negative drops есть and takes the genitive: у меня нет денег.
Можно alone does the work of a whole verb phrase; it is a first-week word in Russian.
To a friend: помоги.
Agrees with the thing owned: чей, чья, чьё, чьи.
'To happen' is случиться or произойти.
Я болею = I'm ill (болею, болеешь). The other болеть, for a body part that hurts, only ever turns up as болит / болят.
Also немножко.
Resting on top of something is на + prepositional.
Motion under takes the accusative: под стол.
'In front of' is перед + instrumental.
Usually just в + prepositional in speech.
'Us' is нас: у нас, для нас, с нами. The verb marks the person, so мы is often dropped: идём!
The odd one out: not *четыредесят.
Just час, never один час.
два/три/четыре часа, but пять часов.
Russian counts half towards the coming hour: полпятого is 4:30, not 5:30.
Instrumental adverbs: утром, днём, вечером, ночью.
отец is formal, or used when talking about someone else's father. Папа is both the everyday word and the way you call him.
мать is formal or used about someone else.
No single word for 'siblings' in everyday speech.

items.en: elder/younger marked by старший/младший before the kin term
items.note: Adjective agrees: старший брат, старшая сестра.
Used for both sides; дед is blunter.
Russian has no separate maternal term; the side is spelled out only when it matters.
Same as above: по маме / по папе is the only marking.

items.en: how you address a mother-in-law: first name + patronymic
items.note: тёща (wife's mother) and свекровь (husband's mother) are reference words, never used to her face; мама once you are close.

items.en: how you address a father-in-law: first name + patronymic
items.note: Reference words are тесть (wife's father) and свёкор (husband's father).

items.en: excuse me (hailing a man you don't know)
items.note: Used at any age. For a woman: девушка. Мужчина/женщина are blunter.
To a group of friends: ребят!
Все = everyone; всё (with ё) = everything.
Warm and casual; да, конечно when you need to be polite.
There is no ghee in Russian cooking; масло on its own at table means butter.
Sunflower oil, подсолнечное, is the default.

Masculine despite the -е ending: чёрный кофе.
'Очень вкусно!' is what you say to the cook.

Plural стулья.

Always plural in form.
Мыться is the general 'wash oneself'; баня is its own event.
In the house people just say свет.
Off is выключить.

items.en: household requests use the perfective imperative; -ка or пожалуйста softens it (закрой-ка дверь)
items.note: Russian's counterpart to the Hindi compound imperative: aspect and the -ка particle carry the politeness, not an extra verb.

items.en: по- + verb: 'go on, have a bit of ...' – the everyday family nudge
items.note: The по- prefix turns an order into an invitation: поешь = have a bite, посиди = sit a while, поспи = get some sleep.
Plural глаза.
Мне холодно – I'm cold; на улице холодно – it's cold out.
The body part is the subject: болит голова, болят ноги.
At the chemist: что-нибудь от кашля / от головы.
Russian treats light blue, голубой, as a separate colour, not a shade.
Dative of кто; 'whom' as object is кого.
Откуда ты? – where are you from?
'Ask me' takes у меня; 'by me' takes мной.
с + instrumental; со before мной for ease of pronunciation.
Casual singular: с тобой.
The shop and café workhorse.
Pronounced 'u nevo'.

Negative commands use the imperfective: не делай, не бери.
Feminine обе.
Very colloquial alternative: вообще.
Carrying it somewhere on foot: отнести.
The thing liked is the subject: мне понравился фильм.
By transport: приедешь.
The fixed-route minibus that fills the auto-rickshaw slot; you call out 'на остановке, пожалуйста'.
Flagging cars down is dying out; nearly everyone uses the Яндекс Такси app.
Also 'exactly' as an agreement noise.
Verb звонить: позвони мне.
'Телефон сел' – my phone's dead.
Да? on its own is normal with friends.

items.en: what's the weather like with you?

items.note: Polite: слушайте. The standard way into a request or a piece of news.

items.en: past tense agrees with the subject's gender and number, not with person
items.note: The past is where agreement bites: person is never marked, so я, ты and он all take сказал – but a woman saying я сказал is an instant giveaway.
Also договорились – agreed, will do.
Shortened to может in speech.

items.en: in the afternoon, during the day
items.note: Russian has no separate word for 'afternoon'; день covers it.
Casual: сейчас.
Russian names the people rather than the household: родители мужа, родня жены, поехали к моим.
Подожди! – hang on. Imperfective ждать.
Also нас разъединило.

items.en: so, what's new? (keeping a call going)

items.note: A woman says я пошла; in a hurry, я побежал.
Отель for smarter places, гостиница everywhere else. Neither ever means a restaurant – that is ресторан or кафе.
Static 'on the right' is справа.
Static 'on the left' is слева.
Adjective лёгкий.
Трудно stresses effort, сложно complexity.
Stress on the first syllable. Also класс! круто!

items.en: used to do: раньше + imperfective past
items.note: No separate habitual tense; раньше or бывало carries the 'used to'.

items.en: was doing: the imperfective past covers both 'was doing' and 'used to do'
items.note: Russian collapses the two Hindi past tenses into one imperfective form.

items.en: have done: the perfective past does the work of the English present perfect
aspect pairs: every verb has an imperfective (process) and a perfective (completed result) – писать/написать, есть/поесть
items.note: This is Russian's version of the Hindi compound-verb colouring, and it is unavoidable from the first week: you cannot form a past or future without choosing.

items.en: having done X: spoken Russian just chains verbs with и or когда
items.note: The true participle (поев, сделав) is written register; using it in conversation sounds like a newsreader.
Agrees: должен, должна, должны. Colloquially мне надо / мне нужно.
Agrees in gender and number with what it refers back to.
Я сам сделал – I did it myself. Feminine сама.
'Not yet' is ещё не.
Also 'I don't mind': мне всё равно.
Weekdays are lower case; 'on Sunday' is в воскресенье.
Feminine полторы: полтора часа, полторы недели.
Also около + genitive: около пяти.
But в следующем месяце / в следующем году.
Russian splits motion from position: сюда (to here) vs здесь/тут (here).
Motion form; position is там.
No side marking. Address form: дядя Ваня.
Only said when the side actually matters.

items.en: дядя/тётя + first name is the address form for any older relative or family friend
items.note: The Hindi system of side-marked kin terms has no Russian counterpart; Russian marks nothing and spells out по маме / по папе when needed.
Feminine соседка.

items.en: bless you, God grant you health (an elder's wish)
items.note: What an older relative says instead of thank you. благословение is strictly religious.
Mates-only version of с днём рождения; Russians do not use an English birthday phrase.

items.en: New Year – the big family festival
items.note: Occupies Diwali's place: tree, family table, gifts. Christmas (7 Jan) is much quieter.
Most families go occasionally rather than weekly; everyday Russian life is largely secular.
Я простудился – I've caught a cold.
Поликлиника is the local clinic you actually visit.
Обижаться is a big social concept; feminine обиделась.

items.en: to go out for a walk, to be out
items.note: Пойдём гулять – let's go out.
играть в футбол (games) but играть на гитаре (instruments).
Dropping someone off by car is подвезти.
Возьми трубку! Picking an object up is поднять.
Inviting properly is пригласить.

items.en: to teach; to learn by heart
items.note: Учиться = to study; учить кого-то = to teach someone.
Russian picks the verb by orientation: положить flat, поставить upright, повесить hanging.
Носить = to wear habitually; быть в + prepositional for what someone has on.
'Вы выходите?' – are you getting off? is the standard question in a packed bus or metro.

items.en: right, I'll let you go – bye
items.note: The standard Russian phone sign-off; давай here means nothing literal.
Fills cricket's role as the sport everyone has an opinion about; хоккей close behind.
Plural. Новость (singular) = a piece of news.
Also the standard answer to 'how are things?' – ticking along.
Не спеши – no rush.
The metro announcement: осторожно, двери закрываются.
'Separately' is отдельно.
Здесь свободно? – is this seat free? Empty is пустой.
Also a discourse marker: так, что дальше?
Сдача is the change handed back to you.
Rarer than in India; more often heard about hot water being off for summer maintenance.
The л is silent: 'sontse'.
Air is воздух.
Indeclinable. In practice everyone orders through the Яндекс Такси app.
Irregular: хочу, хочешь, хочет, хотим, хотите, хотят.
полшестого = 5:30, because Russian counts towards the coming hour.

items.en: respectful greeting to an elder: здравствуйте + first name and patronymic
items.note: The patronymic is the Russian respect marker: a teacher, a doctor or a friend's mother is Мария Ивановна, never just Мария.
Dative subject: мне жарко, мне скучно.
A transport delay is задержка: задержка рейса.
Works for a driver and for someone speaking too fast.
Стою в пробке – I'm stuck in traffic.
On a bus: на следующей остановке, пожалуйста.
The message you send on arrival: доехал, всё хорошо. On foot: дошёл.
Long-distance trains are announced by путь (track number).
Счёт, пожалуйста. Also a bank account and a match score.
Used for flights and long-distance coaches alike.
At the chemist: что-нибудь от кашля.

items.en: 21–99 are two separate words; the noun after a number follows 1 → nominative singular, 2–4 → genitive singular, 5+ → genitive plural (один рубль, два рубля, пять рублей)
items.note: Unlike Hindi's fused numbers, Russian numbers are easy to build but change the noun after them – this rule bites at every till.

items.en: comparative -ее and superlative самый + adjective; 'than' is чем or the genitive
items.note: Он старше меня or он старше, чем я – both fine.
Rare in speech – Russians say the digital time: четыре пятнадцать.
Verb забронировать; у меня бронь на имя ...
A rush-hour crush is давка.
Russia has no everyday traditional dress; шуба is the culturally distinctive winter garment. Сарафан is folk costume only.
A false friend with kurta – куртка is an outdoor jacket.
Обувь = footwear in general; туфли = smart shoes; кроссовки = trainers.
Shoes come off at every Russian front door and slippers (тапочки) are handed to you – identical custom, so this earns an early tier.
Festival greetings all use с + instrumental: с праздником, с Рождеством.
Feminine будь счастлива; older relatives usually say дай Бог здоровья instead.
A cut or wound: я порезался / поранился.
Меня тошнит – no subject, the person goes in the accusative. Actual vomiting is рвота.
У меня аллергия на орехи.
A national conversation topic: у меня давление.
Сахар only in сахар в крови (blood sugar), never on its own for the condition.
Indeclinable.
скинуть is the everyday 'send'; Telegram is what friends use
Colloquial; сфотографировать in full
господи is just as common
A woman says одна
How you get male staff's attention; девушка for a woman
No honorific plural in Russian

items.word: когда я пришёл, он уже ушёл
items.roman: kogda ya prishyol, on uzhe ushyol
items.note: Russian has no pluperfect
пошли? is even more casual
нужен/нужна/нужно/нужны agree with the thing needed
-те for вы
«картой можно?» = can I pay by card?
за домом = behind the house. The commoner за is за + accusative: спасибо за помощь, за тебя! (a toast). Going to fetch something takes the instrumental: сходить за хлебом.
Russian says 'on the street'
без сахара
Colloquial; как is the neutral 'like, as'
Blame-flavoured; благодаря for good causes
куда-нибудь if you're going there
звук = sound, громкость = volume
потише = quieter
было весело = it was fun
нет настроения = not in the mood
Russian counts to the next hour: 'half of the second'
Spoken default; formal «пятнадцать минут шестого»
через + accusative for time from now
утра/дня/вечера/ночи instead of am/pm
'on [day]' = в + accusative; во вторник takes во
A man is женат, a woman замужем
One word for every aunt, either side
двоюродная сестра for a female cousin
Wife's parents are тесть и тёща
Also a brother's wife
Everyday wording; зять is the formal term
Almost nobody says it – «брат жены» in speech

items.en: in-law terms split by whose parents they are
items.note: Husband's parents vs wife's parents; the sibling terms have faded from speech
мои родные
Rare in speech; женщина is the everyday word
Father's name + -ович/-овна; the Russian equivalent of 'sir'
Letters and officialdom only

items.en: excuse me (to a woman); young woman
items.note: How you address any woman up to middle age in a shop
The moment you drop вы with a new friend
«сколько у вас детей?» for how many
сливочное = butter, растительное = cooking oil
Meals are verbs: завтракать, обедать, ужинать
On the table at every meal
гречневая, овсяная – the default breakfast
Served with сметана
The staple side dish

Usually in tea

Tinned, for salads

Russian mustard is fierce; хрен is the other one
Drinking yoghurt, an everyday staple
Homemade; морс is the berry version
минералка = mineral water
Warm and informal; «очень вкусно» is the neutral praise
The line that actually works at a Russian table

Also 'to get in the way'

садитесь to вы

The banya besom is the same word
Colloquial; «мусорное ведро» in full
Colloquially «стиралка»
Also 'morning exercises'
выключатель = light switch
свет горит = the light's on
телефон сломался
Genitive after нет

items.en: did you turn the gas off?

items.note: Always plural
уши in the plural
поясница = lower back
дыхание = breath
Blunt but standard; «расстройство желудка» at the doctor's
In speech you'd say «голова кружится»
слабый = weak
ушиб = bruise, порез = cut
The doctor's opening question
у меня болит голова
простудилась if you're a woman
ушиблась for a woman
Russians 'drink' medicine
Pharmacy frame: от + genitive = for (a complaint)
Adjectives stand alone as nouns: красный = the red one
Dative for how you feel: мне холодно, мне скучно
«ужас!» on its own = how awful
высокий = tall (of people)
тонкий for objects
Also 'hard, tough'
где = where something is, куда = where you're going
Colloquial; «до которого часа» is the tidy version
Also «сколько по времени»
этот declines (этого, этому); the possessive его/её never changes
Accusative/genitive: «меня зовут…», «у меня»
с ней with her
ей to her – dative
«до сих пор» when it's dragged on

items.word: где – там, когда – тогда, какой – такой
items.roman: gde – tam, kogda – togda, kakoy – takoy

перед домом
к врачу, к нам
«одевайся, а то замёрзнешь»
«ни за что!» = no way
извини is the everyday one; -те for вы
The universal spoken filler
вся неделя, всё утро, все дни
«куча народу»; takes the genitive
«он стал врачом» – instrumental
The standard sign-off on a call
Verb of motion + bare infinitive
Rain and snow 'walk': идёт снег
заказать for a table or taxi
Everyone uses the app
Doesn't decline
Street taxis are gone – you agree a price or use the app
«стоять в пробке»; also a cork
Market question: «почём картошка?»
наличными = in cash
How friends settle up – by phone number

items.en: any chance of a better price?
items.note: Markets only – shop prices are fixed
мелочь = small change
Most people just say «телефон»
Doesn't decline
Also the radiator; «зарядка кончается» for a dying phone
«связи нет»
«он в сети» = he's online
«тебя не слышно» for sound
In a Russian flat it's more often «открой окно, душно»
The standard consoling shrug
Texting and speech; short for нормально
нашла if you're a woman
Men shake hands every time they meet – never across a threshold
«не злись» = don't be cross
+ genitive: «я боюсь собак»
поменять when it's done once
Tone decides which
петь = to sing
одна for a woman
Agree the fare before you get in
They behave like adjectives: на шестом этаже
«без пятнадцати» in speech
«вызовите скорую!»; 112 from a mobile
«поверните направо»
Russian reuses где for the relative clause
Resigned shrug
Bookish; пользоваться in speech
ноль is the everyday form
«на выходных» = at the weekend

items.en: dates: ordinal + month in the genitive
items.note: 'On the first of May' = первого мая
«в январе» = in January
Forms and officialdom; жена in speech
«сделать предложение» = to propose
невеста = bride
The polite way to say it
One word for things and people; пожилой is politer for people
«попробуй!» = give it a go / have a taste
Deli counters sell by grams; полкило = half a kilo
«пакет нужен?» at the till
For before the central heating comes on
Hot water is central – every summer «горячую воду отключили»
выйти = to get off

items.en: what would you like to drink?
items.note: The host's offer; «что будете» to вы
Plainer: «давно не виделись»
-те for вы
соскучилась for a woman; «скучаю по тебе» while apart
занята for a woman
свободна for a woman
«как учёба?»
Colloquially «универ»
«по телеку»; телевизор in full
Where you see a GP; больница is a hospital
«колени болят» – a stock complaint
«держи!» = here, take this
«телефон упал»
«налить тебе чаю?»
-то = a particular someone, -нибудь = anyone at all; both decline: кому-то, у кого-нибудь
«он, наверное, дома» – the guessing word
«собираюсь уходить» = I'm about to leave
«поешь как следует»
Russians also sit in silence a moment before a journey: «присядем на дорожку»

items.en: ring me when you get there

items.note: Same word whoever you're praising
«какой милый!»
Handed to you at the door – shoes come off
Flowers expected; 23 февраля is the men's one
Carry it – you can be asked for ID
+ instrumental: «пользоваться телефоном»
Always plural
The safe neutral greeting to anyone from mid-morning until dark, then вечер. доброе утро only holds until about eleven.
The neutral goodbye to anyone you are on вы with. пока is for friends; всего доброго / всего хорошего closes a shop or office exchange.
The opposite of можно: здесь нельзя курить. With the dative it means 'I mustn't': мне нельзя сладкое.
The everyday agreement word. ну ладно wraps a conversation up, and ладно? checks the other person is happy.
Он уже дома. With a negative it flips to 'not any more': я уже не работаю.
ещё чаю? = more tea; он ещё спит = he's still asleep; ещё раз = one more time.

items.en: yes/no questions are made by intonation alone
items.note: No word order change, no auxiliary, no question word. The voice jumps sharply on the word you are asking about and then drops.

items.en: one stressed syllable per word; unstressed о is said as a
items.note: хорошо = харашо, Москва = Масква, сейчас = сичас. The stress also moves inside a word: рука́ but ру́ки.

items.en: ь and е ё и ю я soften the consonant in front of them
items.note: Softening changes the word: мат / мать, угол / уголь, ел / ель. The soft sign is not a sound of its own, it bends the consonant before it.
я ухожу = I'm off; он уже ушёл = he's left. Leaving by vehicle is уезжать / уехать.

items.en: to drop in; to pop into
items.note: зайди в магазин = pop into the shop; я зайду вечером = I'll come round. зайти за кем-то = to collect someone on the way.
Said to anyone about to eat, including strangers at the next table in a canteen. Reply: спасибо.

items.en: how old are you? – мне тридцать лет = I'm thirty
items.note: Age takes the dative: мне, тебе, ему. Then the number bends год: 21 год, 22 года, 25 лет.
бы is what makes it 'would', and it is the politest way to order or ask. Shorter still: мне бы кофе.
заплатить за обед = pay for lunch (за + accusative). At a till: оплата картой, я заплачу.
кафе never declines. столовая is the cheap canteen, and it is where people actually eat lunch.
бокал вина = a glass of wine, кружка пива = a beer. Spirits come out for toasts rather than for sipping.

items.en: it's not working; out of order
items.note: Covers a dead lift, a card reader and a closed counter alike. If it broke just now: сломался.
на следующей остановке = at the next stop. A metro stop is станция, a mainline terminus вокзал.
на улице Ленина = on Lenin Street, and на улице on its own = outside.
Можно вопрос? = can I ask you something? задать вопрос = to ask a question.
Что значит это слово? Plural слова, with the stress on the end.
русский язык, английский язык. The same word is the thing in your mouth.

items.en: to meet for the first time; to get to know
items.note: Приятно познакомиться = pleased to meet you; давай познакомимся opens the introduction. Meeting up with someone you already know is встретиться.

items.word: как доехать до ...? / как пройти к ...?
items.roman: kak doyekhat do ...? / kak proyti k ...?
items.note: доехать if you'll take transport, пройти on foot. до takes the genitive, к the dative.

items.en: excuse me, do you know where ... is?
items.note: The standard way to stop a stranger, softer than скажите. The answer usually starts вон там or прямо и налево.
Closes an arrangement, and is often the last word before пока on the phone.
Gendered: a woman says согласна, a group согласны. я не согласен is not rude, just direct.
по-моему, это дорого. Softer than я думаю and heard far more often.
вообще-то = actually, to be honest; вообще не знаю = no idea at all. It peppers spoken Russian.
идёт снег = it's snowing, the same verb as rain. снег лежит = there's snow on the ground.
Irregular and unavoidable: ем, ешь, ест, едим, едите, едят. One sitting of it is поесть: я уже поел.

items.en: the ending that turns a verb back on its subject
items.note: начинается, находится, нравится, вернулся. It becomes -сь after a vowel: я боюсь, она вернулась.
На каком этаже? Russia counts the ground floor as первый этаж, so a British first floor is второй.

items.en: let's drink to ... / here's to you
items.note: Toasts take за + accusative: за встречу, за хозяйку, за здоровье. Someone proposes one before nearly every glass.

items.word: спасибо, я не пью / я за рулём
items.roman: spasibo, ya ne pyu / ya za rulyom
items.en: no thanks, I'm not drinking / I'm driving
items.note: Both are accepted without argument. Мне хватит stops a refill mid-evening.
будь здоров to a friend. The same phrase doubles as a warm goodbye to an older person.
Кофе с собой is on every kiosk. Eating in is здесь.
Smoking indoors is banned, so the answer to здесь можно курить? is almost always нельзя, только на улице.
Жаль, что не получилось. жалко is the warmer, more spoken one; мне тебя жалко = I feel for you.

items.en: to make it in time; to manage to
items.note: я не успел = I didn't get round to it, or I missed it. Imperfective успевать.
For buildings, streets and offices. For a person or a thing on the table, plain где is enough.
For a lost object it's я потерял; if the thing itself went missing, потерялся.

items.en: two hundred / three hundred / five hundred
items.note: Prices live in hundreds: триста рублей. четыреста and восемьсот are the two that trip people up.
На улице мороз. Temperatures are said as минус двадцать, never with 'degrees'.
Какой у вас размер? = what size are you? Clothes and shoes go by European sizes.
у меня украли телефон – no subject needed, 'they stole'. Emergency number from any mobile is 112.
